question: Who held Messines and Wytschaete on 1 and 2 November?
reading_a: German: Messines from 1 November, Wytschaete from 2 November
reading_b: Both retaken by the French at 11 a.m. on 2 November
evidence_for:
S41, p. 85: by 4 p.m. on 1 November the attackers reached the eastern edge of Wytschaete; fierce street fighting in Messines all day; p. 87: Wytschaete the centre of the heaviest fighting on the 2nd.
S45: the Germans had both by the morning of 1 November.
S40, Sketch 12 (4 November): the French line about 1 km west of Wytschaete.
evidence_against:
S42 Hamilton: "at 11 a.m. on the 2nd, both Messines and Wytschaete were retaken by the French" (page not checked).
S41, p. 85, editors' note: by the afternoon of 1 November the French had taken over the defence of Wytschaete; p. 87: the credit for its defence that day belongs to the French.
adopted_because: French counter-attacks reached the villages without holding them.
history:
Status in Conflicts: Open
what the sources say: S45: the Germans had both by the morning of 1 November. S41: Messines cleared to its western edge on 1 November; Wytschaete entered and lost twice, then taken by 5 p.m. on 2 November. S42: "at 11 a.m. on the 2nd, both Messines and Wytschaete were retaken by the French", and again on 6 November.
how the pilot handled it: German account followed: Messines German from 31 October to 1 November, Wytschaete from 2 November. French line drawn west of both.
comment: Hamilton may be describing French counter-attacks that got into the villages and did not stay.

v7 update: Sketch 12 (4 November) draws the French line about 1 km west of Wytschaete and has the British cavalry and 4th Division well west of Messines. Both villages are German by the 4th on the official map.

question: Did the Germans take Hill 60 on 11 November?
reading_b: Held by the Allies until December
evidence_for:
S41, p. 119: "the capture of Hill 60 near ZWARTELEEN was of exceptional importance".
S40, Sketch 14: the French line on the afternoon of 11 November bent back north of the hill.
evidence_against: No source read. The December date was a recollection of Claude's, recorded as such on 13 Nov.
adopted_because: The German account and the British official sketch agree.
history:
Status in Conflicts: Open
what the sources say: S41: the XV Corps captured Hill 60 near Zwarteleen on 11 November. None of the British sources read mentions it. As far as I know the hill is usually said to have been lost by French troops in December 1914.
how the pilot handled it: Line not moved. Hill 60 left on the Allied side with a note on both rows.
comment: Needs a French source or the later chapters of the British official history.

The German XV Corps row keeps the places the German account names (Klein Zillebeke and the canal bend) and is not carried forward to the hill.

adopted_because: St. Eloi and Zwarteleen are 4 km apart across the canal; S44 may run two events together.
